status_summary: The only action found in the Mandate's direction is at the General Counsel level: on 2025-02-14 the acting General Counsel's memo GC 25-05 rescinded a group of memos, including the guidance on the Board's 2023 Cemex decision that revived bargaining orders without an election. The Board itself has not overruled Cemex: after the Sixth Circuit on 2026-03-06 (Brown-Forman v. NLRB) held that the Board improperly announced the Cemex standard through adjudication and denied enforcement of the Cemex bargaining order (without deciding whether the standard is substantively valid), the Board petitioned for rehearing en banc on 2026-05-11, which a law-firm report reads as a sign the Board will keep applying Cemex. The Senate confirmed a third Republican member on 2026-08-07, giving the Board a 3-1 Republican majority and the three votes that Board practice requires to overrule precedent, and on 2026-08-26 the General Counsel issued memo GC 26-04, which law-firm reports say names Cemex among precedents she intends to ask the Board to revisit, but no Board decision on Cemex or the contract bar, no NLRB rulemaking on recognition procedures or the contract bar and no bill requiring secret-ballot elections exclusively was found. In the Cemex case itself the Ninth Circuit upheld the bargaining order on 2026-04-21 under the older Gissel standard without reaching the validity of the Cemex standard, and the Supreme Court denied certiorari on 2026-10-19 (No. 26-225), so the standard's validity remains undecided by any appellate court.

timeline.event: Acting General Counsel issues GC 25-05, which rescinds a set of earlier memos including GC 24-01 (Revised), the guidance in response to inquiries about the Cemex card-check bargaining-order decision.

Senate confirms Board members James Murphy and Scott Mayer and General Counsel Crystal Carey (53-43), ending a period of nearly a year without a Board quorum; Carey is sworn in as General Counsel and the Board regains a quorum on 2026-01-07 with Democratic member David Prouty.
NLRB publishes its only post-inauguration substantive rule found in the Federal Register through 2026-10-07, on joint employer status; it does not address recognition procedures or the contract bar.

In Brown-Forman Corp. v. NLRB (Nos. 24-2107/25-1060), a divided Sixth Circuit panel (McKeague, Griffin; Mathis dissenting) holds that the Board used adjudication improperly to announce the Cemex bargaining-order standard as a general rule, grants the employer's petition, denies enforcement of the Cemex bargaining order and remands; it upholds the Board's unfair labor practice findings and does not decide whether Cemex is substantively valid.
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit

timeline.event: In Cemex Construction Materials Pacific v. NLRB (No. 23-2302), the Ninth Circuit issues an unpublished memorandum disposition upholding the Board's bargaining order under the traditional Gissel standard, based on the employer's unfair labor practices during the election campaign, and does not reach the Cemex standard itself (per a law-firm blog; the Supreme Court docket lists the Ninth Circuit decision date as 2026-07-01).

The NLRB asks the Sixth Circuit for rehearing en banc in Brown-Forman and, in a Ninth Circuit brief, calls the panel's analysis flawed; a law-firm report expects the Board to keep applying Cemex until courts stop it. No ruling on the petition was reported as of 2026-05-22.

Senate confirms James Macy (Republican) and David Prouty (Democrat, second term) to the Board, producing a 3-1 Republican majority with one vacancy; a law-firm commentator says this lets the Board overturn precedent under its three-vote practice. The report does not mention Cemex or the contract bar.
James R. Macy is sworn in as an NLRB Board member for a term ending 2030-08-27, completing the 3-1 Republican majority that followed the 2026-08-07 confirmations.

The NLRB's General Counsel memo listing shows GC 26-04, 'Further Guidance Regarding General Counsel Priorities,' dated 2026-08-26 (the memo file could not be opened by the research tool). Two law-firm reports describe it as naming Cemex among precedents General Counsel Crystal Carey intends to ask the Board to revisit, with a return to the Gissel and Linden Lumber framework for recognition demands; neither mentions the contract bar. The Board has not acted on it in any decision found.

The Supreme Court denies certiorari in Cemex Construction Materials Pacific v. NLRB (No. 26-225, from Ninth Circuit Nos. 23-2081, 23-2302 and 23-2377; petition filed 2026-08-18, the federal respondent and the union waived responses), leaving the Ninth Circuit's judgment in place without any ruling on the Cemex standard.
